2.1.1.speaker: TUNA
2.1.1.text: Pink Beetle. Plow. Armored doors I did with scrap from a filing cabinet.

2.1.3.speaker: ALI
2.1.3.text: Got on the bus. Cats couldn't.

2.1.4.speaker: TUNA
2.1.4.text: So you stayed for the cats.

2.1.6.speaker: TUNA
2.1.6.text: Deac's gonna like that. Don't tell her I said so.

2.1.8.speaker: TUNA
2.1.8.text: The reason you're not in trouble. Probably. Office is in the back. Knock. She hates it when people don't knock.

2.1.9.speaker: TUNA
2.1.9.text: Hey, girl. Missed you. She's been feeding you the cheap stuff, hasn't she.

2.2.2.speaker: DEAC
2.2.2.text: That's a cat I pulled out of a building you left it in.

2.2.4.speaker: DEAC
2.2.4.text: You made noise. You ran. You took the loud one and forgot the quiet one.

2.2.4b.speaker: DEAC
2.2.4b.text: Then you honked. Every one of them for three blocks. That lot's gone now. Nobody's getting back in there.

2.2.5.speaker: DEAC
2.2.5.text: That's not a judgment. That's a report.

2.2.8.speaker: DEAC
2.2.8.text: I was on the roof across the lot. We watch that building. People still think it works.

2.2.9.speaker: DEAC
2.2.9.text: You stopped at every stop sign on Central.

2.2.11.speaker: DEAC
2.2.11.text: Nobody's ever coming. That's not the point.

2.2.9x.speaker: DEAC
2.2.9x.text: You stopped at every stop sign on Central. Every one.

2.2.9y.speaker: DEAC
2.2.9y.text: Nobody does that anymore. Nobody was coming and you did it anyway. Remember what that felt like.

2.2.12.speaker: DEAC
2.2.12.text: You want fuel, you need a permit. You want a permit, I'm the only one who can give you one this side of the mountains. And I don't sign for people I haven't watched drive.

2.2.14.speaker: DEAC
2.2.14.text: The cat's fine. She sleeps eighteen hours a day and eats like a raccoon.

2.2.15.speaker: DEAC
2.2.15.text: Run deliveries for me. Show me you can keep a convoy alive. Then we talk about the cat.

2.2.18.speaker: ALI
2.2.18.text: What if I just take her.

2.2.19.speaker: DEAC
2.2.19.text: Then you've got two cats, no fuel, and a very nice car parked in Kent forever.

2.2.20.text: Mya opens one eye. Looks at Ali. Closes it.

2.2.22.speaker: DEAC
2.2.22.text: No. She's not. Tuna's got a bay for you. Be here at six.

2.3a.brief.speaker: DEAC
2.3a.brief.text: Insulin. Pharmacy safehouse on Meeker. I'm riding.

2.3.3.speaker: DEAC
2.3.3.text: I know. I say it anyway. Go.

2.3a.Q1.w1.speaker: DEAC
2.3a.Q1.w1.text: That's a highway. This is a stop sign. First to stop, first to go. Again.

2.3a.Q1.w2.speaker: DEAC
2.3a.Q1.w2.text: You're in a Beetle with a plow. Think about what you just said. Again.

2.3a.Q2.w1.speaker: DEAC
2.3a.Q2.w1.text: Left. Sure. Go trade paint with the other person who thought left. Again.

2.3a.Q2.w2.speaker: DEAC
2.3a.Q2.w2.text: Nobody's waving. Nobody's ever waving again. Again.

2.3.8.speaker: DEAC
2.3.8.text: Person on the right. Out here nobody's coming, but you do it anyway. Habits are the only thing that outlive you.

2.3.9.speaker: DEAC
2.3.9.text: No sign. What do you do.

choices.text: Slow down. Look. Yield to the right.
Stop and wait for someone to wave you through.

2.3a.Q3.w1.speaker: DEAC
2.3a.Q3.w1.text: Get through it. Into what. Again.

2.3a.Q3.w2.speaker: DEAC
2.3a.Q3.w2.text: You'll be sitting there a long time. It's not a stop sign. It's a look-both-ways sign that nobody bothered to put up. Again.

2.3.10.speaker: ALI
2.3.10.text: Slow down. Look. Yield to the right.

2.3.13.speaker: DEAC
2.3.13.text: {GRANDMA_NAME}. She failed her renewal vision test in '09 and argued with me for forty minutes.

2.3.16.speaker: DEAC
2.3.16.text: That's it. Squeeze it. They don't care about you. They care about the car.

2.3a.red.speaker: DEAC
2.3a.red.text: Stop. Foot off everything. Let them forget.

2.3.19.speaker: DEAC
2.3.19.text: Pharmacy. Insulin goes to the woman with the clipboard. Don't slam the door.

2.3.22.speaker: ALI
2.3.22.text: She says "I know" like it's a threat.

2.3a.slam.text: The door slams. Across the lot, heads turn.

2.3a.swarm2.speaker: DEAC
2.3a.swarm2.text: That's not a failure. That's a Tuesday. Warehouse. We go again.

2.3b.title: Delivery 2 — Cat Food to Auntie Bea

2.3b.brief.speaker: DEAC
2.3b.brief.text: Cat food. Bea. The dock's tight — you'll be backing in. Nobody watches you back up. Do it like they are.

2.3.23.speaker: ALI
2.3.23.text: Mirrors. Check both. Check over the shoulder. The mirrors lie about how much room there is.

2.3.24.speaker: ALI
2.3.24.text: Slow. Slower than that. Backing is the only time everyone forgives you for going slow.

2.3b.bump.speaker: ALI
2.3b.bump.text: — that's a dumpster. That was a dumpster. Okay. Fading. Mirrors, Ali.

2.3b.clean.speaker: ALI
2.3b.clean.text: Straight. Nobody heard. Bea heard. Bea's allowed.

2.3.25.speaker: BEA
2.3.25.text: Oh, you're the Beetle girl. Deac's been impossible about you.

2.3.27.speaker: BEA
2.3.27.text: She hasn't said a word. That's how I know. Come in, come in, mind the door, Pickles is right there.

2.3.28.speaker: BEA
2.3.28.text: This is the sanctuary. Eleven cats. Twelve if you count the one that lives in the ceiling, and I do.

2.3.30.speaker: BEA
2.3.30.text: Silent. Hear the Quiet before you do. Ever notice your fat one wake up for no reason?

2.3.32.speaker: BEA
2.3.32.text: It's never no reason. Now. That orange one of yours.

2.3.34.speaker: BEA
2.3.34.text: I have a collar. No bell. Soft clip. And I have toys, which is what she actually needs. A busy cat is a quiet cat. Trade Points, sweetheart. Nothing's free but advice.

2.3c.brief.speaker: DEAC
2.3c.brief.text: Radio parts to Priya. Central Avenue. Three lanes, all of them empty. Signal anyway.

2.3.35.speaker: ALI
2.3.35.text: Signal first. Then mirror. Then shoulder. Then move. Signal early enough that if there were anyone alive to see it, they'd have time to care.

2.3c.nosig.speaker: ALI
2.3c.nosig.text: No signal. Nobody saw. Doesn't matter. Habits.

2.3.36.speaker: PRIYA
2.3.36.text: Are those the capacitors? Tell me those are the capacitors.

2.3.38c.speaker: PRIYA
2.3.38c.text: Box is not lying. You're my favorite person today. Don't tell Jonah, he gets weird.

2.3.40.speaker: ALI
2.3.40.text: I don't know what that is.

2.3.41.speaker: PRIYA
2.3.41.text: Oh, honey. Four idols in the Tacoma Dome bunker. They broadcast at nine p.m. on 91.3. Everything's whisper-level — they had to, it's the rule — and it turned into this whole thing. Whole bunker sings along under their breath. You've never heard anything like it.

2.3.42.speaker: PRIYA
2.3.42.text: I trade photocards. Radio skins for your dash. Lightbar colors. Sori's the rare pull, don't let anyone tell you different. Trade Points. Come back at nine and I'll tune you in.

2.3d.brief.speaker: DEAC
2.3d.brief.text: Filters to Tuna. His dock. Parallel.

2.3.43.speaker: ALI
2.3.43.text: Pull up alongside. Back until the mirror lines up. Cut the wheel. Straighten when the front clears. {GRANDMA} made me do this in the Fred Meyer lot forty times.

2.3.44.speaker: TUNA
2.3.44.text: Little tighter — no, you got it. You got it.

2.3d.curb.speaker: TUNA
2.3d.curb.text: Curb. Everybody heard that. Again. Slow. She'll wait.

2.3d.clean.text: The Beetle settles against the dock. Nothing squeals.

2.3.47.speaker: TUNA
2.3.47.text: Every Sunday. I watched her teach half of Kent in that lot.

2.3.48.speaker: TUNA
2.3.48.text: Okay. Shop's open. Quieter muffler — that's ten decibels you never have to worry about again. Better rubber for the pass. Lights for the dark. Chains. You'll need chains. Everybody thinks they don't need chains.

2.3.49.speaker: TUNA
2.3.49.text: And I can tune the plow. Right now it's a wall. I can make it a wedge. Still loud. Always loud. It's a last-resort tool, kid. Not a strategy.

2.4.brief.speaker: DEAC
2.4.brief.text: Milk run. Pharmacy and back. Jonah's out there somewhere. Don't let him make you do anything.

2.4.pre.text: A van blows through the intersection ahead, tires squealing. Every one of the Quiet on the corner turns.

2.4.2.speaker: ALI
2.4.2.text: My grandma drove this car for forty years and never woke anybody up.

2.4.5.speaker: JONAH
2.4.5.text: I'm Jonah. I'm the fast one.

2.4.7.speaker: JONAH
2.4.7.text: Deac says you're the careful one. She says it like it's a compliment. She doesn't say anything about me like it's a compliment.

2.4.9.speaker: JONAH
2.4.9.text: Maybe stop being right. See you at the warehouse, Grandma.

2.4.14.speaker: ALI
2.4.14.text: I think that was a compliment. I think that was the whole compliment.

2.4.alt1.speaker: JONAH
2.4.alt1.text: Oh, you woke 'em up too. Nice. We're twins.

2.4.alt3.speaker: JONAH
2.4.alt3.text: I start a lot of things. Name's Jonah. I'm the fast one.

2.4.alt5.speaker: JONAH
2.4.alt5.text: See you at the warehouse. Try not to bring the whole corner with you.

2.4.alt14.speaker: ALI
2.4.alt14.text: …That was not a compliment. That was the whole not-compliment.

2.6.buy_toy.speaker: BEA
2.6.buy_toy.text: A busy cat is a quiet cat. She'll hate it for an hour and then it'll be her whole life.

2.6.buy_collar.speaker: BEA
2.6.buy_collar.text: No bell. She'll never know it's there. Neither will they.

2.6.buy_snacks.speaker: BEA
2.6.buy_snacks.text: Oh, she'll get up for these. Briefly.

2.6.buy_any.speaker: BEA
2.6.buy_any.text: Good choice. The cats approve. Well — Pickles approves. Pickles approves of everything.

2.6.cant.speaker: BEA
2.6.cant.text: Sweetheart, I'd give it to you. I would. But then everyone would want it for free and the cats would starve. Come back with points.

2.7.buy_sori.speaker: PRIYA
2.7.buy_sori.text: Oh my god. Oh my god. Don't tell Jonah. Do not tell Jonah.

2.7.buy_skin.speaker: PRIYA
2.7.buy_skin.text: That dash is going to look so good. Take a picture. Nobody takes pictures anymore.

2.7.buy_lightbar.speaker: PRIYA
2.7.buy_lightbar.text: Lumi's color. Keep it dim on the road — pretty is fine, bright is a problem.

2.7.buy_any.speaker: PRIYA
2.7.buy_any.text: Yes. Good. Nine p.m. Don't forget.

2.7.cant.speaker: PRIYA
2.7.cant.text: I feel that in my soul. Run something for Deac and come back. The cards aren't going anywhere. Well. Sori might.

2.8.buy_muffler.speaker: TUNA
2.8.buy_muffler.text: Ten decibels. That's ten decibels of not-dying. Best money you'll spend.

2.8.buy_tires.speaker: TUNA
2.8.buy_tires.text: Grip's the whole game. Nobody thinks about grip until they don't have it.

2.8.buy_leds.speaker: TUNA
2.8.buy_leds.text: You'll see farther. Doesn't mean you can go faster. Means you can stop in time.

2.8.buy_plow.speaker: TUNA
2.8.buy_plow.text: Wedge, not wall. Still loud. Still last resort. Say it back to me.

2.8.buy_any.speaker: TUNA
2.8.buy_any.text: Good. She'll like that. She doesn't say so, but I can tell.

2.8.cant.speaker: TUNA
2.8.cant.text: Run some more deliveries. She'll wait. She's good at waiting. She waited two years under a tarp.

lines.speaker: BEA
lines.text: Come in, mind the door. Who needs what?

lines.speaker: BEA
lines.text: How's the orange one? Still a menace? Good. Means she's healthy.

lines.speaker: BEA
lines.text: Pickles has been asking about you. Well. Sitting near the door. Same thing.

lines.speaker: PRIYA
lines.text: Nine p.m. Don't forget. Ninety-one point three.

lines.speaker: PRIYA
lines.text: New cards came in with the Tacoma run. I haven't looked. I'm being strong.

lines.speaker: PRIYA
lines.text: Jonah was in here asking about Sori. I said nothing. I said so much nothing.

lines.speaker: TUNA
lines.text: How's she running? Don't lie, I can hear her.

lines.speaker: TUNA
lines.text: Chains. I'm going to say chains every time you walk in until you buy chains.

lines.speaker: TUNA
lines.text: Hey, kid. Hey, girl. (That second one was the car.)

lines.speaker: ALI
lines.text: Signaled to nobody. Felt great. Doing it again.

lines.speaker: DEAC
lines.text: Then you didn't lose anything that matters. Warehouse. Try again.
